findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not IsInSource within the compilation. Diagnostics created with a null location (e.g. FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() yielding null, or Location.None) are silently dropped. This also changes behavior for existing same-assembly cases where a diagnostic was previously reported with a location-less/None location (e.g. type-level diagnostics using GetIdentifierLocation that returns null for partial/unusual declarations). Users could lose diagnostics (MsgPack003/004/005 etc.) they previously saw.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] type whose diagnostic location resolves to null/Location.None in the same compilation (e.g. via GetIdentifierLocation returning null) - assert the diagnostic is still reported on head as on base. Also run the full analyzer test suite (MsgPack003-018) for regressions.

findings.claim: Wrapping reportDiagnostic changes filtering for ALL diagnostics globally, not just metadata types. A diagnostic whose location is in a syntax tree from the compilation but obtained from a different compilation instance (e.g. generator-produced trees, or the compilation passed to TypeCollector differing from the analyzer's compilation) is now dropped. This is a broader filter than the crash fix required.

receipt_plan.detail: Read TypeCollector constructor and callers that pass a compilation: confirm the compilation used in ContainsSyntaxTree is the same one whose trees produce diagnostic locations; compare reported diagnostics in the existing analyzer test suite on base vs head.

findings.claim: The MemberNeedsKey / key-is-null check is now skipped entirely for types without declaring syntax. Closed generic types from metadata whose members lack [Key] no longer produce anything. This is consistent with L8, but the guard also skips the AOTDerivedKeyAttribute diagnostic and the subsequent logic in that block; any non-diagnostic side effect in that block (e.g. suppress/continue behavior) for metadata types is changed, possibly altering which members are included in the generated formatter for the closed generic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator snapshot tests with a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly having an unkeyed public member; compare the generated output on base (crash-free variant) vs head to verify the member set is unchanged.
